steps.title: Sign in
steps.internal: Authentication validates the session credentials. The model is not involved in deciding identity.

steps.title: Open authenticated chat
steps.internal: Server resolves customer DEMO-A. All later requests use its validated session, not a caller-selected customer ID.

steps.title: Ask about a declined payment
steps.internal: API accepts the message, assigns a turn sequence and request/conversation references.

steps.title: Persist the conversation turn
steps.internal: Persist accepted conversation event. Optional capture is durable; current banking data is not written into semantic memory.

steps.title: Read preferences and working context
steps.internal: Coordinator reads permitted preference version 7 and working context. No card is selected yet.

steps.title: Clarify which card
steps.internal: Authorized product summaries are obtained through the gateway. The scenario has one matching declined payment per card, so card selection disambiguates the task. If still ambiguous, ask another question.

steps.title: Select the Visa card
steps.internal: Backend resolves the display reference to canonical CARD-DEMO-01 within the customer’s products. A suffix never serves as the primary key.

steps.title: Request authorized card/payment data
steps.internal: Model/coordinator requests registered enquiry tools. Gateway validates arguments and checks operation permission and product ownership.

steps.title: Retrieve recorded transaction facts
steps.internal: Provider reads the synthetic bank records: TX-DEMO-17, INR 2,000, declined, recorded reason “merchant restriction”. If no reason is recorded, the answer must say so.

steps.title: Retrieve the applicable policy
steps.internal: Separate policy retrieval filters the synthetic corpus by product and effective date. Policy evidence explains procedure; it does not invent the transaction’s cause.

steps.title: Explain the recorded reason
steps.internal: Context builder combines permitted facts and sources. The model explains them; response checks reject unsupported amounts or a claim that settings were changed.

steps.title: Change the durable language preference
steps.internal: Interpret as a durable preference correction, not a bank-profile change. Assign source event sequence 19.

steps.title: Accept preference event and outbox
steps.internal: Commit event 19 and an outbox record before durable acceptance. Session overlay can use Hindi while projection processing is pending; do not claim saved yet.

steps.title: Apply the validated preference
steps.internal: Worker claims durable work, validates key/value/scope and applies the projection transaction with event-order/version checks: Hindi, version 8, last sequence 19.

steps.title: Reject an older late update
steps.internal: Inject the planned fault: an older English extraction with source sequence 17 completes after event 19. Version/order check rejects it; no rollback of the newer intent.

steps.title: Confirm the saved preference
steps.internal: API/UI reports persisted only after the projection commit is observed. This is a proposed interaction, not a measured working implementation.

steps.title: Ask to raise a support case
steps.internal: Use the scoped transaction reference, not a remembered status. Gather any required issue details and prepare an operation proposal.

steps.title: Show the proposed case summary
steps.internal: Proposal records the exact normalized fields, principal, operation and validity. Display the preview in the current preferred language.

steps.title: Confirm the exact proposal
steps.internal: Confirmation binds to this principal and proposal. An edit, expiry or changed session invalidates it.

steps.title: Check authority and replay record
steps.internal: Gateway reauthorizes the operation/resource and checks a principal/operation/payload-bound idempotency key. New execution requires valid proposal confirmation.

steps.title: Commit one case and its evidence
steps.internal: Local support service transaction commits CASE-DEMO-1042, its success audit, idempotency result and domain-event outbox together. Memory processing is not required for this commit.

steps.title: Simulate a lost response
steps.internal: Inject response loss after commit. This is unknown from the UI’s perspective, not evidence the write failed. Preserve the same operation reference.

steps.title: Retry the same operation
steps.internal: Through the authenticated API, the gateway rechecks access and matching payload. A completed replay returns the recorded result without executing a new write; consumed confirmation cannot authorize a different operation.

steps.title: Return the original receipt
steps.internal: Return the original authorized receipt. Do not create a second case or a second successful mutation. A replay may have its own operational log.

steps.title: Update permitted conversation context
steps.internal: Outbox consumer records an allowed case reference or summary with source provenance. Case status remains authoritative in the support backend; do not persist a stale “Open” status as preference truth.

steps.title: Return in a new session
steps.internal: Validate a fresh session and customer. The simulator advances through a declared event: the case becomes “Under review”. This is an illustrative status, not a promised bank SLA.

steps.title: Recover preference and case reference
steps.internal: Retrieve Hindi preference version 8 and permitted historical case reference. If multiple cases match, clarify. Revalidate reference ownership; memory alone is not permission.

steps.title: Fetch current case status
steps.internal: Gateway authorizes the case lookup. Provider reads current support state. Do not answer from the remembered creation receipt.

steps.title: Return current support evidence
steps.internal: Validated provider evidence returns through the gateway to the coordinator/context builder. The diagram abstracts return hops; authorization remains in force.

steps.title: Explain the latest update in Hindi
steps.internal: Compose the answer from current support evidence and preference version 8. Trace, audit-relevant events and evaluation results stay separate.
